entities.summary:
Étienne de Vignolles, Sieur de Montmorillon, Chatelain de Longueville, also known as La Hire, was a French military commander during the Hundred Years' War.

    La Hire led the French forces to several victories against the English, including the Battle of Crécy in 1346 and the Battle of Poitiers in 1356.

    His military campaigns helped establish the French monarchy's dominance in Western Europe, paving the way for the rise of the French nation-state.

    La Hire's legacy extends beyond his military achievements, as he played a significant role in shaping the development of French chivalry and the feudal system.

    In his later years, La Hire became a prominent figure in the French nobility, serving as the Constable of France and playing a key role in the governance of the kingdom.

    La Hire's life and career serve as a testament to the enduring impact of medieval warfare on the course of European history.
